subject: TangentISV gateway: technical adoption gate and validation timeline
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bates <simon.bates@tangentisv.com>
Cc: partners@tangentisv.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TangentISV gateway: technical adoption gate and validation timeline

Hi Simon —

Thanks again for the product demo last week. Tangent's gateway looks promising and the partnership team is keen to move this to a technical validation spike so we can confirm production compatibility and generate a recommended reference architecture.

Proposed scope for the validation (2-week spike):
- Connectivity and auth (mutual TLS + bearer token flow)
- Request/response contract stability for streaming generation endpoints
- Latency profiling at 1x/5x baseline traffic
- Fallback behaviour when connector returns 5xx or malformed payloads
- Small catalog of regressions using the provided test prompts

Success criteria (binary gate):
1) End-to-end pipeline runs in our staging VPC with < 2% 500s under 1k qps equivalent;
2) No modifications required to Redwood request schema beyond header mapping;
3) Clear fallback defined and exercised in canary run.

Can you confirm the names of the engineers on your side and whether you can provide an S3 test bucket + sample payloads? We can run the first compatibility sweep the week of Jun 18–22 — I can host a kickoff on Mon 18 at 10am PT if that works.

I attached a brief reference architecture draft (redwood-ref-arch-v1.md) to help speed alignment.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-ref-arch-v1.md (markdown, 12KB)]

From: Simon Bates <simon.bates@tangentisv.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TangentISV gateway: technical adoption gate and validation timeline

Hi Vanessa —

Great to hear — we're aligned to run the spike. Engineers joining on our side: Priya Nambiar (protocols) and Elliot Moore (backend). We can stand up an S3 bucket and put together a small corpus of sample requests; I'll share access by end of day Friday.

Quick notes on our side that will shape the plan:
- Auth: we support mTLS and a signed bearer-token header (X-TG-Auth) — we prefer mTLS for production but bearer for initial smoke.
- Streaming: our gateway supports SSE-style streaming chunks; we can also stream NDJSON over HTTP/2 if you need per-token latency info.
- Rate limits: default per-connection throttling is 2k rps; can be adjusted for canary.

Mon 18 10am PT works for a kickoff — I'll send a calendar invite.

Simon
Director, Integrations
TangentISV

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-06-15T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: TangentISV gateway: technical adoption gate and validation timeline — internal prep

Team —

Per Simon, Priya and Elliot from Tangent will join. Kickoff 2028-06-18 10:00 PT (calendar invite pending). Goals for our internal prep:
- Karthik: prepare a compatibility matrix to capture header mapping, auth flows, expected status codes, streaming modes (attach matrix).
- Marissa: plan a minimal SLO/latency experiment and set up traffic generator in staging (1x and 5x baseline).
- Sergio: coordinate customer success for any change to request schema and note rollback plan.

Please keep items small and actionable — this is a two-week focused effort. I've attached Vanessa's reference arch and I want the matrix by EOD 6/16 so Tangent can populate the fields.

Cheers,
Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Simon Bates <simon.bates@tangentisv.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-16T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Compatibility matrix + clarifying questions

Simon / Vanessa / Marissa —

I've attached the compatibility matrix (tangent-compat-matrix.xlsx). A few clarifying items raised while building the fields: 
1) Auth fallthrough — if we attempt mTLS and it fails, do you expose a clear 401 with an error code we can reliably detect, or do you terminate the connection? We need deterministic observable behaviour for the fallback policy.
2) Streaming framing — is SSE the canonical mode? If you support NDJSON over HTTP/2, can you confirm chunk boundaries and keep-alive semantics?
3) Response envelope — for multi-part answers, are token-level deltas included as separate events or aggregated in the final body?
4) Error classification — can you map which errors we should treat as transient (retry) vs permanent (fallback to model variant)?

If you can drop short answers inline in the matrix or reply here I'll reconcile quickly.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: tangent-compat-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)]

From: Simon Bates <simon.bates@tangentisv.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-17T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility matrix + clarifying questions — initial test sweep results

Karthik / Vanessa —

Thanks for the matrix; we've filled several fields and pushed a short test sweep this morning. Attaching the raw log (tangent-test-results.log). Highlights:
- mTLS handshake succeeds for 95% of connections in our lab; we saw two intermittent TLS timeouts (both traced to a transient cert fetch race).
- SSE streaming delivered chunked tokens but our consumer library coalesced small packets under load — implication: per-token latency appears higher than wire-level.
- One failure: when Redwood sends a late cancel (client abort), our gateway currently returns 502 instead of an explicit aborted event. This will cause Redwood's retry-fallback code to believe the request failed and attempt a variant fallback.

Proposed mitigation for the gateway: add an explicit aborted event mapping to 499 and include an error-code header (X-TG-ERR) for owners. We can patch a canary tomorrow and re-run.

Attaching logs: tangent-test-results.log

Simon
Director, Integrations
TangentISV
[Attachment: tangent-test-results.log (log, 112KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Simon Bates <simon.bates@tangentisv.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-18T16:41:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Compatibility matrix + clarifying questions — follow-ups and gate decision

Simon / team —

Thanks for the quick sweep and the diagnostic log. Summary and next steps from Redwood's side:
- Karthik: we'll interpret the 502-on-cancel as a gating item. If Tangent can patch to emit 499 + X-TG-ERR by the canary retest tomorrow, we will consider the streaming/fallback behaviour resolved.
- Marissa: proceed with the latency SLO experiment once Simon confirms the canary patch is live. Capture 95th/99th token latencies and token-per-second throughput.
- Sergio: update CS runbook to include rollback to our hosted fallback (model-variant + caching) and share with Tangent.

Tentative gate decision: if the canary patch reduces abort-misclassification and 99th-token latency stays within the expected tolerance during the 5x load run, we green-light a reference-arch signoff and schedule a production canary for Jul 9. Otherwise, we'll extend the spike one week to address regressions.

Simon — appreciate the quick turnaround. Please drop a short note when the canary with the 499 mapping is live and I'll re-run the sweep with Marissa's harness.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partner Solutions
Redwood Inference
